title: Convert a Logo to SVG
description: Turn a raster logo file into a clean, scalable SVG ready for print, web, embroidery, and cutting.
steps: Upload your PNG or JPG logo to the converter.
Select 'Logo & Clipart' from the preset menu for clean, solid-color output.
If the background is not transparent, enable 'Remove Background' in settings.
Click Convert and wait a few seconds.
Download the SVG and open it in Illustrator, Figma, or Cricut Design Space.
tips: Using a transparent PNG as input (instead of a white-background JPG) skips the need for background removal.
If the logo has gradients, the 'Gradient' preset preserves them better than 'Logo & Clipart'.

title: Vectorize an Image for Cricut
description: Prepare any raster image — sketch, clipart, or photo — as a cuttable SVG for Cricut Design Space.
steps: Upload your image to the converter.
Select the 'Cricut / Vinyl' preset to get clean cut-path outlines.
Enable 'Remove Background' if your image isn't already on a transparent background.
Convert and download the SVG.
Import the SVG into Cricut Design Space — it will appear with ready-to-cut contours.
Optionally use our SVG Optimizer to merge overlapping paths before cutting.
tips: High-contrast clip art works best. Photographs often need cleaning up first.
If you get too many small stray paths, increase the 'Noise Threshold' slider before converting.

title: Batch Convert a Folder of Images
description: Process dozens of PNG or JPG files at once with consistent settings and download as a single archive.
steps: Open the Batch Converter.
Drag your folder of images into the upload zone, or click to select multiple files.
Choose common settings — format, preset, background removal — applied to every file.
Click 'Start Batch' and watch the progress bar.
When complete, download individual results or click 'Download All' for a zip archive.
tips: Sort your files before uploading — results preserve the original filename so sorting is easy.
Background removal adds 0.25 credits per file; disable it for images that are already clean.

title: Remove a Background Before Vectorizing
description: Isolate your subject with AI background removal, then convert the transparent PNG to a crisp vector.
steps: Open the Background Remover.
Upload your photo — product shot, logo scan, or illustration.
The AI isolates the subject and outputs a transparent PNG.
Download the PNG or click 'Vectorize this' to send it straight to the converter.
In the converter, choose the 'Photo' or 'Illustration' preset and convert.
tips: Photographs with busy backgrounds benefit most — the AI handles hair and fur edges better than a manual path.
If the subject has a gradient, choose 'Gradient' in the vectorizer so it blends smoothly.

title: Prepare a Laser Cutting File
description: Convert a sketch or design into a laser-ready DXF or SVG with clean, single-stroke cut paths.
steps: Scan or photograph your design on a clean, white background.
Upload to the converter and select the 'Technical / Line Art' preset.
In Advanced Settings, enable 'Single-stroke outline' for cut paths rather than filled shapes.
Choose DXF as the export format for LightBurn, RDWorks, or LaserGRBL.
Import the DXF into your laser software, set power/speed, and cut.
tips: Draw in black on white paper for the cleanest trace — pencil grey causes false paths.
Add a 0.1mm kerf offset in your laser software to compensate for beam width.

title: Upscale a Low-Res Image First
description: Improve vectorization accuracy by using the AI upscaler on small or blurry source images before tracing.
steps: Open the Upscaler and upload your image.
Choose 4x for very small images (under 300×300 px) or 2x for moderately sized ones.
Download the upscaled image, or click 'Vectorize this' to pass it straight to the converter.
In the converter the AI now has four times more pixels to work with, producing sharper paths.
tips: AI upscaling adds detail that wasn't in the original — the goal is a better trace, not more information.
For logos, 2x is usually enough; for photographs go for 4x if the original is under 500 pixels wide.

title: Optimize an Existing SVG
description: Reduce SVG file size and clean up messy paths from other tools, so the file is leaner for web and email.
steps: Open the SVG Optimizer.
Upload an SVG exported from Illustrator, Figma, or another tool.
Review the savings report — it shows which optimization passes will shrink the file.
Click Optimize to remove unused defs, inline redundant styles, and reduce decimal precision.
Download the optimized SVG — typical savings are 30–70%.
tips: Avoid running the optimizer on SVGs with embedded animations — some minification passes can break keyframe references.
Always keep a backup of the original before optimizing.
